01 / The context

A problem worth exploring.

Readers want to understand the ideas behind AI papers without losing the detail inside equations, architecture diagrams, and terminology.

A Claude Code skill that turns AI research papers into interactive HTML lessons with analogies, workflows, annotated code, plain-English math, and quizzes.

Mini-lesson / weighted attention

A reading group with different voices.

Imagine asking a question in a reading group. You listen more closely to the people whose notes are relevant. Attention similarly combines information with different weights. This analogy explains weighting, not every detail of a Transformer.

03 / Decisions & evidence

Behind the experience.

Approach & boundaries

The skill guides a coding assistant to analyze a paper and produce a self-contained HTML lesson. Teaching patterns include analogies, annotated code, equation explanations, and scenario-based quizzes. Inspired by Zara Zhang’s codebase-to-course skill, as credited in the original LinkedIn post; this project specializes in research papers.

MarkdownHTMLCSSJavaScript

What the evidence shows

The README includes example output for Attention Is All You Need. The interactive lesson on this page was written for the portfolio to illustrate the skill’s teaching patterns; it was not generated by running the skill.
